recipes.title: Rails: Consent Mode v2 banner and loader with CSP nonce
Rails: exceptions_app ErrorsController rendering 404/410/422/429/500/503 inside the layout
recipes.snippet:
Rails 8.x. `config.exceptions_app` (set to the router, wrapped in the CSP middleware) makes Rails re-dispatch every rescued exception as GET / into your router, so ErrorsController renders INSIDE the layout with the real status. Delete public/404.html, public/422.html, public/500.html (static defaults, fingerprinted by shipgate). Unknown routes (RoutingError) and ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound (find / find_by!) are already mapped to 404 by Rails; ActionController::TooManyRequests to 429. Keep the layout free of database queries: the 503 page renders while the database is down. Needs `<%= yield :head %>` in the layout head (headers recipe) and a root route. Production needs consider_all_requests_local = false (the default). Merge the rescue_from into your existing ApplicationController. ### file: config/application.rb module MyApp class Application < Rails::Application # The exceptions app runs outside the middleware stack, so wrap it in the CSP middleware or error pages lose their # Content-Security-Policy header (SEC-010). Same env, so the nonce in the page matches the header. config.exceptions_app = ActionDispatch::ContentSecurityPolicy::Middleware.new(self.routes) end end ### file: config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do root "pages#home" get "/old-pricing", to: "errors#gone" # RTE-004: retired path with no successor answers 410 # keep LAST: the exceptions app asks for /404, /500, ... get "/:code", to: "errors#show", constraints: { code: /404|406|422|429|500|503/ } end ### file: app/controllers/errors_controller.rb class ErrorsController < ApplicationController def show # Only the exceptions app (which stores the exception) may render these; a direct visit to /500 is a plain 404. raise ActionController::RoutingError, "Not Found" unless request.env["action_dispatch.exception"] @status = params[:code].to_i render :show, status: @status, formats: :html # the real status, never 200 end def gone @status = 410 render :show, status: :gone, formats: :html end end ### file: app/controllers/application_controller.rb class ApplicationController < ActionController::Base # RTE-007: a dependency failure is 503, never 404 and never a 200 shell. rescue_from ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished, ActiveRecord::QueryAborted, with: :service_unavailable private def service_unavailable(exception) Rails.logger.error("database unavailable: #{exception.class}") # log only, never rendered @status = 503 response.headers["Retry-After"] = "30" render "errors/show", status: :service_unavailable, formats: :html end end ### file: app/views/errors/show.html.erb <% content_for :head do %><% end %>
<%= link_to "Back to the home page", root_path %>
<% title = case @status when 404 then "Page not found" when 410 then "This page has been removed" when 422 then "Your session expired. Reload the page and try again." when 429 then "Too many requests" when 503 then "Temporarily unavailable" else "Something went wrong" end %>

<%= title %>

<%= @status == 503 ? "Please try again shortly." : "You can go back to the home page and continue from there." %>

recipes.title: Rails: contact form with authenticity_token, rate_limit, honeypot and webhook delivery
recipes.snippet:
Rails 8.x, no extra gem. Env: FORM_WEBHOOK_URL. Append the honeypot rule to your existing app/assets/stylesheets/application.css. CSRF: form_with adds the authenticity_token and Rails' forgery protection (on by default) rejects a missing or wrong one (422 page). Abuse limit: Rails' built-in controller rate_limit (per IP, 429 TooManyRequests) needs a SHARED cache store in production (Solid Cache or Redis; a per-process memory store resets and splits the count); behind a proxy make sure request.remote_ip is the visitor (config.action_dispatch.trusted_proxies). Success is shown only after the webhook answered 2xx; any failure or timeout is a 502. Needs the error-pages recipe for the 422/429 pages. For a stronger bot check replace the honeypot with Cloudflare Turnstile (cf-turnstile-response verified server-side). ### file: config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do get "contact", to: "contacts#new", as: :contact post "contact", to: "contacts#create" get "contact/thanks", to: "contacts#thanks", as: :contact_thanks end ### file: app/models/contact.rb class Contact include ActiveModel::Model include ActiveModel::Attributes attribute :name, :string attribute :email, :string attribute :message, :string # Server-side validation and length limits. validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 100 } validates :email, presence: true, length: { maximum: 254 }, format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP } validates :message, presence: true, length: { maximum: 5000 } end ### file: app/controllers/contacts_controller.rb require "net/http" class ContactsController < ApplicationController protect_from_forgery with: :exception # SEC-024 rate_limit to: 5, within: 10.minutes, only: :create # SEC-054: the 6th POST in the window is answered 429 def new @contact = Contact.new end def create # SEC-055 honeypot filled: same response as success, no side effect. return redirect_to(contact_thanks_path, status: :see_other) if params[:company_website].present? @contact = Contact.new(params.expect(contact: [:name, :email, :message])) return render(:new, status: 422) unless @contact.valid? if deliver(@contact) redirect_to contact_thanks_path, status: :see_other # POST/redirect/GET, works without JavaScript else @delivery_failed = true # RES-008: never show success for a failed delivery render :new, status: :bad_gateway end end def thanks; end private # REPLACE this method's body with your destination (CRM API, email provider, DB insert); keep the 2xx check and timeouts. def deliver(contact) uri = URI.parse(ENV.fetch("FORM_WEBHOOK_URL")) http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port) http.use_ssl = uri.scheme == "https" http.open_timeout = 3 http.read_timeout = 8 http.write_timeout = 8 post = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json") post.body = contact.attributes.to_json http.request(post).is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess) rescue Timeout::Error, SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse => e Rails.logger.error("contact delivery failed: #{e.class}") false end end ### file: app/views/contacts/new.html.erb

Contact us

<% if @delivery_failed %>

We could not send your message. Please try again later.

<% end %> <% if @contact.errors.any? %>
    <% @contact.errors.full_messages.each do |message| %>
  • <%= message %>
    • <% end %>
<% end %> <%= form_with model: @contact, url: contact_path do |f| %>

<%= f.label :name, "Name" %> <%= f.text_field :name, autocomplete: "name", required: true, maxlength: 100 %>

<%= f.label :email, "Email" %> <%= f.email_field :email, autocomplete: "email", required: true, maxlength: 254 %>

<%= f.label :message, "Message" %> <%= f.text_area :message, required: true, maxlength: 5000, rows: 6 %>

<%= label_tag :company_website, "Leave this field empty" %> <%= text_field_tag :company_website, nil, tabindex: -1, autocomplete: "off" %>

By sending this form you agree to our Privacy notice.

<%= f.submit "Send message" %> <% end %>
### file: app/views/contacts/thanks.html.erb

Thank you

Your message was sent.

### file: app/assets/stylesheets/application.css /* honeypot: visually hidden but NOT type=hidden, so naive bots still fill it */ .hp-field { position: absolute; left: -10000px; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; }

recipes.title: Rails: CSP with per-response nonce, security headers, HSTS and immutable asset cache
recipes.snippet:
Rails 8.x. Rails' own mechanisms: CSP DSL with its nonce generator, default_headers, force_ssl + ssl_options. Do NOT use the permissions_policy initializer DSL: in actionpack it still emits the legacy Feature-Policy header in the old syntax, so Permissions-Policy is sent through default_headers instead (SEC-010). HTML already gets Cache-Control "max-age=0, private, must-revalidate" from Rails (nothing to add). Hashed assets (Propshaft/Sprockets digests) get immutable below; public_file_server.headers applies to EVERY file in public/, so keep non-hashed files (favicon.ico, robots.txt) out of public/ or serve them from a route/CDN rule.
### file: config/initializers/content_security_policy.rb
Rails.application.configure do
  config.content_security_policy do |policy|
    # Resulting header (SEC-010 / SEC-075):
    #   default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'strict-dynamic' 'nonce-<random>'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-<random>';
    #   img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self';
    #   form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests
    policy.default_src :self
    policy.script_src  :self, :strict_dynamic
    policy.style_src   :self
    policy.img_src     :self, :data
    policy.font_src    :self
    policy.connect_src :self
    policy.object_src  :none
    policy.base_uri    :self
    policy.form_action :self
    policy.frame_ancestors :none
    policy.upgrade_insecure_requests true if Rails.env.production?
  end

  # A fresh random nonce per response (not the session id), stamped on script-src and style-src.
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_generator = ->(request) { SecureRandom.base64(16) }
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_directives = %w[script-src style-src]
end
### file: config/application.rb
module MyApp
  class Application < Rails::Application
    config.load_defaults 8.0

    # Rails already sends nosniff and Referrer-Policy; restated so a changed default cannot regress them.
    config.action_dispatch.default_headers.merge!(
      "X-Content-Type-Options" => "nosniff",
      "Referrer-Policy" => "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
      "Permissions-Policy" => "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
    )
  end
end
### file: config/environments/production.rb
Rails.application.configure do
  config.force_ssl = true # https redirect, secure cookies and Strict-Transport-Security
  # config.assume_ssl = true # only when the TLS-terminating proxy does NOT send X-Forwarded-Proto (it disables the redirect)
  config.ssl_options = {
    hsts: { expires: 63_072_000, subdomains: true }, # max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains
    redirect: { exclude: ->(request) { request.path == "/api/health" } } # plain-http probes from the load balancer
  }

  # PRF-008: digest-named assets never change.
  config.public_file_server.headers = { "cache-control" => "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" }
end
### file: app/views/layouts/application.html.erb
<head>
  <%= csrf_meta_tags %>
  <%= csp_meta_tag %>
  <%= yield :head %>
  <%= stylesheet_link_tag :app %>
  <%= javascript_include_tag "application", nonce: true, defer: true %>
</head>

recipes.title: Rails: /api/health with a database check (not rails/health#show)
recipes.snippet:
Rails 8.x (ActiveRecord::Base.with_connection is 7.2+). Do not use the built-in `rails/health#show` (/up) for this: it only proves the app booted (green page, no database check) and answers 500 on failure; keep /up for the container orchestrator if you like. This controller inherits ActionController::Base directly, so no layout, auth, allow_browser or CSRF filters apply. The body is a fixed literal: no versions, no adapter names, never the exception. No database in the project: replace the SELECT 1 with a call to your critical dependency and keep the rescue. Also set `database.yml` connect_timeout / checkout_timeout (about 2) so a dead database fails fast.
### file: app/controllers/health_controller.rb
class HealthController < ActionController::Base
  def show
    # OPS-002: process AND database reachable. Timeout bounds a hung connection.
    Timeout.timeout(2) do
      ActiveRecord::Base.with_connection { |connection| connection.select_value("SELECT 1") }
    end
    render_health "ok", :ok
  rescue StandardError => e # includes Timeout::Error and ActiveRecord connection errors
    Rails.logger.error("health check failed: #{e.class}") # log only, never in the body
    render_health "unavailable", :service_unavailable
  end

  private

  def render_health(status, http_status)
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    render json: { status: status }, status: http_status
  end
end
### file: config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get "api/health", to: "health#show"
end
### file: config/environments/production.rb
Rails.application.configure do
  # Load-balancer probes carry the container's own Host header and use plain http.
  config.host_authorization = { exclude: ->(request) { request.path == "/api/health" } }
  # also exclude "/api/health" from the https redirect: see ssl_options in the headers recipe
end

recipes.title: Rails: robots.txt, sitemap.xml and X-Robots-Tag driven by DEPLOY_ENV
recipes.snippet:
Rails 8.x. DEPLOY_ENV and SITE_URL are read from ENV when the app boots (no build-time inlining; assets:precompile does not freeze them). Only DEPLOY_ENV=production means production. DELETE public/robots.txt (and any public/sitemap.xml): Rails serves files from public/ before the router, so a static file shadows the route. Sitemap is a controller + Builder view (Builder escapes every value); for large sites generate it with the sitemap_generator gem instead. The middleware sits outside the whole stack so static files and error pages carry X-Robots-Tag too (non-production only).
### file: config/initializers/deploy_env.rb
# IDX-005: DEPLOY_ENV is the only switch. Every non-production response says "do not index".
Rails.application.config.x.production_deploy = ENV["DEPLOY_ENV"] == "production"

class NoindexMiddleware
  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
    headers["x-robots-tag"] = "noindex, nofollow"
    [status, headers, body]
  end
end

unless Rails.application.config.x.production_deploy
  Rails.application.config.middleware.insert_before 0, NoindexMiddleware
end
### file: config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get "robots.txt", to: "robots#show"
  get "sitemap.xml", to: "sitemaps#show", defaults: { format: "xml" }
end
### file: app/controllers/robots_controller.rb
class RobotsController < ApplicationController
  def show
    lines =
      if Rails.configuration.x.production_deploy
        ["User-agent: *", "Allow: /", "Disallow: /api/", "Disallow: /admin/", # never disallow /assets/ or other CSS/JS/image paths
         "", "Sitemap: #{ENV.fetch('SITE_URL').chomp('/')}/sitemap.xml"]
      else
        ["User-agent: *", "Disallow: /"] # no Sitemap line outside production
      end
    render plain: lines.join("\n") + "\n" # text/plain
  end
end
### file: app/controllers/sitemaps_controller.rb
class SitemapsController < ApplicationController
  # Replace with the public, indexable, canonical pages (200, not noindex); same trailing-slash policy as the canonical tags.
  PATHS = %w[/ /about /contact].freeze

  def show
    raise ActionController::RoutingError, "Not Found" unless Rails.configuration.x.production_deploy # 404 outside production

    site = ENV.fetch("SITE_URL").chomp("/")
    @urls = PATHS.map { |path| "#{site}#{path}" }.uniq
    raise "more than 50,000 URLs: write a sitemap index" if @urls.size > 50_000 # IDX-004
  end
end
### file: app/views/sitemaps/show.xml.builder
xml.instruct!
xml.urlset(xmlns: "http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9") do
  @urls.each do |url|
    xml.url { xml.loc url }
  end
end
